tonight.headline: Wilson is cleared — the lineup stands
body: Bad news first: Stefon Diggs' 20.3 from Thursday is on your bench, and the Wilson-for-Diggs swap now needs Garrett Wilson to beat it from the WR slot. Second: Nicky Jam fixed their lineup at 23:54Z Saturday — Corum, Pollard and A.J. Brown in, Walker and Tate out — so ESPN's edge fell from 80% to 67% (148.1 to 116.5).

Good news: Wilson cleared the concussion protocol this morning and will play (Ian Rapoport via NBC Sports, 15 Nov 12:31Z), and Denzel Boston, his cover, is expected to play 'barring a surprise' (Jeremy Fowler via DraftSharks, 12:19Z). ESPN still tags both questionable — the tag lags the news. The lineup as set is the projection lineup. Nothing to tap; glance at the 10:30 CDMX inactive list to confirm Wilson, because this run is before the official list.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Daniels' 20.8 is banked. A.J. Brown (12.6) plays first, in Munich at 08:30 CDMX — ESPN flipped him from questionable to active at 13:05Z, after this brief's snapshot. Bijan Robinson (18.7) is their biggest number; Coker (11.3) sits on their bench.

case.label: Your check
case.body: Wilson and Boston both land on the 10:30 CDMX inactive lists. Both were reported in this morning; if either surprise, the fallback is DK Metcalf, who kicks off at 19:20 and stays movable after the noon games lock.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A surprise inactive for Wilson at 10:30 — then Boston, or Metcalf if Boston sits too. The margin is about 32 projected points, so losing takes a bust on your side as well as a big Robinson day.

doFirst.subtitle: Wilson was cleared this morning and starts. This only fires if the 10:30 list says otherwise.

case.label: The check
case.body: Rapoport: Wilson 'cleared the NFL's concussion protocol and will play' (NBC Sports 15 Nov 12:31Z). ESPN still shows QUESTIONABLE and 12.8 — the tag has not caught up. This run is before the official inactive list, so the call is provisional: re-check at 10:30 CDMX.

case.label: The cover
case.body: Boston (12.8, toe) practised once, limited, and was in a walking boot Friday; Fowler now has him expected to play 'barring a surprise' (DraftSharks 15 Nov 12:19Z). If both sit, Metcalf (10.6) plays Sunday night at Cincinnati.

case.label: Who is throwing
case.body: Wilson: Geno Smith, not on the Jets' report. Boston: Deshaun Watson starts (clevelandbrowns.com). Metcalf: Aaron Rodgers; Freiermuth (illness) and Harmon are the only Steelers with a status (steelers.com 14 Nov).

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Wilson is inactive and Metcalf outscores Boston after Boston was chosen. The Tuesday Wilson-for-Diggs swap is graded separately: it closes WRONG if whoever fills the slot scores under Diggs' 20.3.

whatWentWrong.title: Diggs scored 20.3 on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: The Tuesday swap put Wilson in on a 2.0 projection edge. Diggs then drew 10 targets and scored the winner.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Wilson 12.8 against Diggs 10.8 on Tuesday — exactly 2.0, labelled PROJECTION. Diggs: 10 targets, 6 catches, 20.3 (archive), the late touchdown in a 24-21 win (VAVEL 12 Nov).

case.label: Why it was still the call
case.body: Diggs played Thursday, so the slot had to be set before Wilson's status was known. The projection lineup is the policy; the backtest found nothing that beats it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wilson (or his cover) scores 20.3 or more — then the swap closes RIGHT. Below it, WRONG on the outcome. Either way it is one decision, not a pattern.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nine weeks of data. The tool prints the same four receivers as Saturday against Diggs, your weakest movable receiver (10.7 a game); nothing at running back or tight end.
